text:
The best combo depends on your **largest load**. A roof air conditioner needs a much bigger station than a fridge, lights and laptops. Pick the tier that matches your RV.

## 1. Weekend trips and light loads (fridge, lights, CPAP, laptops)
**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + two 200W panels**
- 1,024Wh LiFePO4 battery, 1,800W output (3,600W surge), about 28 lb
- 1,000W solar input across two 500W inputs, so you can add panels later. About 70 minutes to full in strong sun with 1,000W of panels.
- 56-minute AC recharge, expandable to 5kWh
- Source: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- Buy: [EcoFlow official store](https://us.ecoflow.com)

*Lighter alternative:* The **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, 23.8 lb) is often sold bundled with SolarSaga panels. It's capped at 400W of solar and can't be expanded. ([source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), buy at [Jackery](https://www.jackery.com))

## 2. Multi-day boondocking (no AC)
**BLUETTI AC200L + 400–800W of panels**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W solar input
- Built-in **30A RV outlet**, so you can plug the RV in directly
- Heavy at about 62 lb
- Sources: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Buy: [Bluetti official store](https://www.bluettipower.com)

*Alternative:* The **EcoFlow Delta 2 Max** (2,048Wh, about $1,499) recharges very quickly from campground power and expands to 6kWh. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))

## 3. Running the roof air conditioner
A 13,500 BTU roof unit draws about 1,500W while running and spikes past 3,000W when it starts. You need 3,000W or more of continuous output.
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3:** 4,096Wh, 4,000W output (8,000W surge), expandable past 12kWh, and quiet. It runs a roof AC for roughly 2.3 hours on one battery. It's heavy enough that moving it takes two people. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)) Buy: [EcoFlow](https://us.ecoflow.com)
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro:** 3,024Wh, 3,000W output (6,000W surge), and starts a roof AC without a soft-start kit. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)) Buy: [Jackery](https://www.jackery.com)

**Budget big-battery option:** The **ALLPOWERS R4000** has 3,456Wh, 3,600W output at 120V, 2,000W solar input, an RV outlet and a 5-year warranty.
- $1,499, or $1,319.12 with code **EXTRA12** (12% off orders over $1,200, expires Nov 15)
- It weighs about 99 lb (45 kg), so it's a "stays in the bay" unit.
- Reaching 2,000W of solar requires panels on all three inputs (650W max each).
- ALLPOWERS says sale items can't be returned.
- Buy: [dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link from the deal site. ([source](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Solar-pairing tips
- **Don't buy more panels than the station's solar input can accept.** A 1,000W rooftop array on a 400W-input station wastes most of its output. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))
- Check the panel voltage and current against each input's limits, especially when wiring panels in series.
- A 300–400W folding array will refill a mid-size (about 2kWh) unit in a full day of good sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- To feed your RV's shore power inlet, use a TT-30 adapter. Get a licensed electrician for anything hardwired.

**My default pick for most RVers who aren't running AC:** a DELTA 3 Plus or AC200L with 400W of folding panels. Tell me what appliances you run and how long you boondock, and I can size it more precisely.
